paragraphs: Lidl is a big supermarket company. It will spend €420 million in Munster, in the south of Ireland.
The plan will create more than 500 new jobs. About 250 of them will be in Cork.
Lidl will open 14 new shops in Munster. It will also make 10 old shops better. The building work will give jobs to many builders too.
In Cork, it will build a large new warehouse at Little Island. This will cost €200 million. Lidl already has more than 6,300 workers in Ireland.
The Taoiseach, Micheál Martin, was happy with the news. He said it was good for jobs, local food suppliers and towns.

The supermarket chain Lidl has announced that it will invest €420 million in Munster. The company says the plan will create more than 500 permanent jobs, bringing its workforce in the region to 1,800.

Lidl will open 14 new stores in Munster and improve 10 existing ones. About 250 of the new jobs will be in Cork, where the company will spend €306 million. This includes €200 million for a new distribution centre in Little Island.
The building work is expected to support 4,500 construction jobs at 25 sites. Lidl also buys a lot of food from local firms. Last year it spent €136 million with 120 suppliers in Cork.

The Munster plan is part of a €600 million investment across Ireland, which includes 35 new stores. Lidl already employs more than 6,300 people in 192 shops, its head office in Tallaght and its distribution centres.
Taoiseach Micheál Martin welcomed the news. He said companies like Lidl help jobs, local suppliers and communities all over the country.
Lidl is to invest €420 million in Munster, a move the discount supermarket says will create more than 500 permanent jobs and increase its workforce in the province to 1,800.

The plan involves opening 14 new stores and redeveloping 10 existing outlets. Cork will receive the largest share, €306 million, including €200 million for a new distribution centre in Little Island, and about 250 of the new roles will be based in the county.

The company expects the projects to support 4,500 construction jobs across 25 developments. It also highlighted its links with local producers, saying it spent €136 million with 120 Cork suppliers last year.

The Munster spending forms part of a wider €600 million investment in the Republic, including 35 new stores. Lidl currently employs more than 6,300 people across 192 stores, its Tallaght head office and its distribution centres.

Chief executive Robert Ryan said the investment showed how important Cork was to the company's future. Taoiseach Micheál Martin welcomed the expansion, saying such businesses support jobs, suppliers and communities nationwide.
Lidl has unveiled plans to pour €420 million into Munster, an expansion the discount grocer says will generate more than 500 permanent jobs and swell its regional workforce to 1,800.

The programme encompasses 14 new stores and the overhaul of 10 existing outlets. Cork is earmarked for the lion's share, €306 million, of which €200 million is set aside for a new distribution hub in Little Island; roughly 250 of the new posts will be located in the county.

The retailer anticipates that the projects will sustain 4,500 construction jobs across 25 developments. It was also keen to underline its ties with local producers, having spent €136 million with 120 Cork suppliers last year.

The Munster outlay is part of a broader €600 million push across the Republic encompassing 35 new stores. Lidl already employs upwards of 6,300 people across 192 stores, its Tallaght headquarters and its distribution centres.

Chief executive Robert Ryan said the commitment underscored Cork's pivotal role in the company's future, while Taoiseach Micheál Martin hailed the expansion as a boost for jobs, suppliers and communities nationwide.
